hints: Focus on the word always in each statement, one counterexample is enough to rule an option out.
Remember that combustion always makes new strong bonds in CO2 and H2O, so it releases heat, while many formations and other reactions can absorb heat.
Think about what happens in every neutralisation, H+ plus OH- joining to make water, and whether bond making there releases or absorbs energy.
walkthrough:
**Recall what the sign means**

Think of negative as exothermic (heat released to surroundings) and positive as endothermic (heat absorbed). We need to test each type of enthalpy to see if its sign is fixed.

Sign rule:
$$\Delta H < 0 \text{ exothermic, } \Delta H > 0 \text{ endothermic}$$

**Test reaction, combustion and formation**

Reactions can be either exothermic or endothermic, so reaction enthalpy is not always negative. Combustion is burning in oxygen and always gives out heat, so it is always negative, not positive. Formation of one mole from elements can be exothermic or endothermic, so it is not always positive.

**Test neutralisation**

Strong acid plus strong base neutralisation is essentially the same ionic reaction every time:
$$\text{H}^{+}(aq) + \text{OH}^{-}(aq) \rightarrow \text{H}_{2}\text{O}(l)$$
Forming the O-H bond in water releases energy, so this is always exothermic with $\Delta H$ negative, about $-57 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$. This is the only statement that is always correct.

options.A: Incorrect. Enthalpy of reaction covers all reactions, both exothermic (e.g. combustion) and endothermic (e.g. thermal decomposition of CaCO3). It cannot always be negative.
options.B: Incorrect. Combustion is burning in oxygen to form very stable oxides like CO2 and H2O. A lot of energy is released when those strong bonds form, so combustion is always exothermic and always negative, not positive.
options.C: Incorrect. Enthalpy of formation can be negative (e.g. formation of CO2) or positive (e.g. formation of NO). It depends on the balance of bonds broken and made, so it is not always positive.
options.D: Correct. Neutralisation of an acid by a base always includes H+ + OH- forming H2O. Bond formation releases energy, so the process is always exothermic and Delta H is always negative.
